strengths: Addresses important practical problem of video understanding efficiency with strong empirical results (95% token compression with minimal accuracy loss across 6 benchmarks)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple benchmarks, baselines, ablations, and efficiency metrics (72% GPU memory, 23.9% latency reduction)
Sound technical design combining event-based retrieval with RL-based distillation; memory-aware compression respects semantic boundaries
Results demonstrate superiority over compression baselines (65% improvement over ByteVideoLLM, 31% over MovieChat) and competitive/superior performance vs. larger models
Reasonable reproducibility with implementation details, hyperparameter validation through ablations, and concrete experimental setup
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: event segmentation, cosine-similarity frame merging, and GRPO are all existing techniques; C-GRPO is primarily GRPO with added retention reward (incremental contribution)

Insufficient justification of key choices: only 5K training instances without data efficiency analysis; fixed top-k=3 across all benchmarks without sensitivity ablations; minimal performance differences for τ (41.34→42.20→41.40) despite claims of validation

Incomplete experimental analysis: missing ablations on retrieval sensitivity (varying k), embedding model choice, computational cost of VMR, failure modes on non-event-structured videos; reference to 'Appendix ??' indicates missing content
Weak generalization validation: trained/validated only on Qwen2.5-VL-3B; minimal architecture diversity in baselines; unclear transfer to different VLM designs

Unexplained efficiency gaps: 23.9% latency reduction is modest relative to 95% token reduction; 72.4% GPU memory reduction but only 11.1% end-to-end latency improvement suggests visual encoding (not LLM) is bottleneck; practical deployment benefit unclear

Methodological comparison concerns: arbitrary token matching (≈120 tokens) for spatial methods; VideoMME shows only 74% retention under extreme compression with limited analysis; inconsistent compression targets across baselines

Presentation issues: Figure 1 duplicated with different captions; unclear when VMR is applied (training/inference/both); hyperparameter m not specified; overstated claims (groundbreaking, exceptional) for incremental work

strengths: Strong empirical results: Achieves 42.20 mean accuracy (99.98% of 42.21 baseline) while reducing visual tokens by 95%, with 72% GPU memory reduction and 23.9% latency improvement across 6 benchmarks

Comprehensive evaluation: Tests on diverse benchmarks (VSI-Bench, VideoMMMU, MMVU, MVBench, TempCompass, VideoMME), with detailed ablation studies, failure case analysis, and fair baseline comparisons

Well-motivated approach: The retrieve-then-compress pipeline is intuitive, with VMR grounded in cognitive science principles (event segmentation, episodic memory), and C-GRPO thoughtfully designed with retention ratio feedback and correctness gating
Practical impact: Addresses real deployment challenges for video VLMs in resource-constrained environments with clear efficiency gains measured on actual hardware
Solid technical execution: Two-stage memory-aware compression respects VMR structure, retention ratio formulation is reasonable, and implementation details are thorough with plans for reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: VMR uses existing TransNet v2 event detection plus standard contrastive retrieval with minimal innovation; C-GRPO is essentially GRPO + one compression reward term; the retrieve-then-compress pipeline represents straightforward combination of existing ideas

Incomplete component analysis: Table 2 shows VMR alone achieves 45.56 vs 42.21 baseline (8% gain), but the paper inadequately explains why retrieval improves full-frame models or what constitutes 'query-relevant' clips beyond retrieval similarity

Test-time overhead unaccounted: Figure 5 efficiency measurements exclude VMR computational cost (event detection, embedding, nearest neighbor search), potentially understating actual latency; end-to-end timing including retrieval stage not reported

Significant performance degradation on long videos: VideoMME achieves only 74% retention (39.44 vs 53.55), contradicting abstract's 'nearly identical accuracy' claim; limitation inadequately addressed in main text and suggests method brittleness to video length

Methodological concerns: C-GRPO trained on only 5K samples with 63% image data that 'will not contribute to compression reward'; sparse correctness gating (Eq. 8) provides weak training signal early on; top-k=3 choice for VMR retrieval lacks justification or sensitivity analysis
Incomplete efficiency evaluation: Latency/memory measurements only on MMVU benchmark; no breakdown of VMR component costs; no measurement of actual compression stage execution time

Fair comparison questions: MovieChat/VidCom/ByteVideoLLM reproduced under artificially matched token budgets rather than their intended operating regimes; SFT baseline trained on different dataset (Video-R1-COT-165K vs Video-R1-260K)
Missing statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs reported; small performance differences lack significance testing; only single seed experiments
